purpose.primary: Represent the theorem stage in the project lineage between earlier triadic structures and later RTT and AACCC development.
purpose.educational: Use selected theorem artifacts to expose definitions, mappings, assumptions, formalization choices, proof boundaries, and unresolved relationships.
purpose.principle: Formalization does not merely ask whether a claim can be proved. It also asks what must be defined before the claim becomes precise enough to prove.

theorem_family.name: Nawderian Temperature Engine Theorem
theorem_family.primary_formalization_problem: What follows from a deliberately simplified directional relation?

theorem_family.name: Unified Resonance Theorem
theorem_family.primary_formalization_problem: What algebraic structure must be supplied for the composition to behave as intended?

nawderian_theorem.name: Nawderian Theorem
nawderian_theorem.shared_membership_interpretation: Dimension 6 is a shared member of the declared groups.

wrapping_claim.source_role: Proposed relationship connecting the wrapping triad with visible and invisible structures.
wrapping_claim.problem: Ordinary set membership alone does not supply the intended semantics of the term wrapping.
wrapping_claim.required_next_step: Define the wrapping relationship before treating it as a formal containment theorem.

prove: relationships directly supported by declared membership
do_not_invent: a convenient definition of wrapping merely to make a stronger theorem pass
formal_response.condition: Only after the intended semantics of Wraps have been defined and justified.

aaccc.awareness: What sets and memberships were actually declared?
aaccc.alignment: Which dimensions actually correspond or intersect?
aaccc.coherence: Does ordinary set containment support the proposed wrapping relationship?
aaccc.clarity: What must wrapping mean before the relationship becomes formally inspectable?
aaccc.continuity: Can the intended conceptual relationship survive a more precise definition?

nawderian_set_theorem.name: Nawderian SET Theorem
nawderian_set_theorem.educational_focus: Decomposition and recomposition of a modeled total into named contributions.
inspection_questions: Which mathematical term corresponds to which proposed contribution?
What happens when one contribution becomes zero?
What assumptions make addition an appropriate composition?
Does the modeled total contain exactly the contributions intended by the teaching model?

formal_boundary.lean_may_verify: Consequences of the explicitly declared additive teaching structure.
formal_boundary.lean_does_not_establish: That the SET decomposition is a complete empirical description of a physical system.
formal_boundary.principle: Formal composition and physical completeness are separate claims.

aaccc.alignment: Which term corresponds to which proposed contribution?
aaccc.coherence: Does the total follow from the supplied composition rule?
aaccc.clarity: Are the individual contributions visible rather than hidden inside an unexplained result?
aaccc.continuity: What happens to the total when one contribution changes while the others remain fixed?

temperature_engine_theorem.name: Nawderian Temperature Engine Theorem

source_interpretation.gradient: driver in the proposed temperature-force relation

teaching_simplification.purpose: Inspect a small algebraic relation before attempting broader physical formalization.

formal_consequences.result: modeled force changes sign under the supplied relation

temperature_engine_theorem.boundary: These are algebraic consequences of the teaching definition and are not independent empirical verification of broader Temperature Engine interpretations.

aaccc.awareness: What quantities and relationships were actually formalized?
aaccc.alignment: How does the gradient sign correspond to the modeled force sign?
aaccc.coherence: Do the zero and sign-reversal properties follow from the declared definition?
aaccc.clarity: Is the simplified algebraic model clearly separated from the broader physical interpretation?
aaccc.continuity: What changes as the gradient changes while the formal relationship remains fixed?

unified_resonance_theorem.name: Unified Resonance Theorem

declared_factors.S_dim: symbolic overlay from a dimensional layer

unified_resonance_theorem.formalization_problem: Compact multiplication notation does not by itself define the types, operation, or algebraic laws required by a proof assistant.
required_questions: Do the factors share a carrier type?
Which algebraic properties are actually required?

boundary.lean_may_verify: Consequences under the explicitly supplied local algebraic laws.
boundary.lean_does_not_establish: That the broader Unified Resonance interpretation naturally or empirically forms this algebra.
boundary.principle: Added formal assumptions remain part of the model and must not be retroactively attributed to the source.

aaccc.awareness: What three factors did the source actually declare?
aaccc.alignment: Which formal object corresponds to each source factor?
aaccc.coherence: What algebraic properties are required before the composition behaves as intended?
aaccc.clarity: Can source declarations be distinguished from assumptions added by the teaching model?
aaccc.continuity: Which consequences survive when factors, carrier types, or composition rules change?

problems.question: What follows from the simplified signed directional relation?
What algebra must be supplied for the composition?

cross_theorem_formalization.shared_lesson: Formalization exposes what must be defined, typed, assumed, or simplified before a theorem can be meaningfully checked.

missing_definition_boundary.principle: An intuitively meaningful word may still lack sufficient formal semantics.
missing_definition_boundary.rule: Do not select one merely because it makes the desired result provable.

added_assumptions_boundary.principle: Compact notation can hide algebraic assumptions.
added_assumptions_boundary.rule: When the formal model adds laws such as associativity or identity, preserve those additions explicitly.

simplification_boundary.principle: A teaching formalization may intentionally model only a narrow portion of a larger source claim.
acceptable_if: the verified consequence is described narrowly
the formal result is not upgraded into validation of the broader claim

formal_refusal.principle: A formal system's inability to establish a stronger claim can be useful information.

example.supported: Dimension 6 belongs to several declared groups.
example.not_automatically_supported: The wrapping group contains the union of visible and invisible groups under ordinary set containment.

formal_refusal.response: Expose the additional definition or assumption required rather than hiding the gap.

questions: What came directly from the source?
source_alignment.purpose: Preserve provenance between source language and teaching formalization.

formal_verification_vs_empirical_validat.formal_question: Given these definitions and assumptions, does this conclusion follow?
formal_verification_vs_empirical_validat.empirical_question: Does the model adequately describe the relevant real-world evidence?

compiler_provenance.boundary: Compiler acceptance applies to the formal teaching artifacts under the stated environment and does not establish the broader empirical claims of their source documents.

change_experiments.question: Does the shared intersection or membership relationship still hold?
What changes in the modeled total?

change_experiments.change: Reverse the gradient or set coupling to zero.
change_experiments.question: Which modeled consequences change or persist?
Which proof obligations can no longer be discharged?

strengthening_claims.principle: Ask the formal system for a stronger theorem and inspect what additional definitions or assumptions become necessary.
strengthening_claims.warning: Do not equate addition of convenient assumptions with stronger empirical evidence.

weakening_claims.question: What is the strongest claim the current structure actually supports?
weakening_claims.principle: A smaller honest theorem may be preferable to a dramatic theorem supported only by convenient assumptions.

questions_after_success: Does the theorem still represent the original intended claim?

awareness: What did the source actually state?
What did the formal model actually define?
alignment: Does the formal representation correspond to the source concept?
Where is the mapping approximate or partial?
coherence: Do the conclusions follow from the formal definitions and assumptions?
clarity: Can source material be distinguished from modeling choices?
Can assumptions be distinguished from proof results?
continuity: What persisted from informal concept to notation to formal model to theorem?

origin_self_inspection.principle: AACCC should be able to inspect the project lineage from which it emerged.
origin_self_inspection.boundary: An origin artifact is not exempt from criticism because it contributed to the later framework.

must: Keep the four theorem families structurally distinct.
Separate source declarations from teaching abstractions.
Expose undefined terminology rather than silently formalize it.
Expose algebraic assumptions added during formalization.
Distinguish formal consequences from empirical claims.
Preserve failed or unsupported stronger mappings as informative boundaries.
Treat compiler validation as validation of the formal artifacts under the stated environment.
must_not: define wrapping merely to make a theorem pass
claim ordinary set containment supports a relationship when the represented sets do not
claim the SET additive teaching model establishes physical completeness
claim the simplified Temperature Engine formalization validates the broader physical interpretation
claim Unified Resonance source notation itself supplies all required algebraic laws
retroactively attribute teaching-model assumptions to the source
upgrade compiler success into empirical validation

do_not_infer: complete formal equivalence between source and teaching model
historical influence beyond documented project lineage
